findings.title: Import reconciliation omits launches outside the lease window
findings.diagnosis: V4 promises closure-blocking detection of an omitted HMA call, but only examines ledger runs whose start time falls inside a lease window. A visible late launch after expiry is excluded rather than classified unauthorized. Checking one-to-one IDs and the envelope digest also does not establish that a matching reservation was valid at the actual launch time. Replay intentionally skips current lease checks. The response supplies an ID and expiry, but the controller contract names only nonzero/missing-response refusal; current-authority handling after revocation is not defined.

evidence.observation: Host omission is promised detectable at import; scan is restricted to start time inside lease window.
Literal v4 import filter detects an inside-window unreserved launch and ignores a visible after-expiry unreserved launch.

findings.reproduction_or_attack: 1. Approve unit U with lease window [10,20). 2. A scheduler resumes late at time 21 and accidentally launches D without the HMA call. Keep the genuine ledger entry visible in the declared namespace. 3. Import the journal and ledger. D is outside [10,20), so the written scan never asks for its reservation. No hidden ledger or forged receipt is needed. Variant: reserve D before a human rewind, delay launch until after revocation, then import a matching ID; v4 does not require comparing actual launch time with authority history.
findings.expected: Detect every observed implementation launch associated with the HMA-bound controller/unit, including launches outside valid authority intervals. A late, revoked or unreserved launch must append a closure-blocking finding. Historical replay must not represent fresh launch permission.
findings.actual: V4 promises closure-blocking detection of an omitted HMA call, but only examines ledger runs whose start time falls inside a lease window. A visible late launch after expiry is excluded rather than classified unauthorized. Checking one-to-one IDs and the envelope digest also does not establish that a matching reservation was valid at the actual launch time. Replay intentionally skips current lease checks. The response supplies an ID and expiry, but the controller contract names only nonzero/missing-response refusal; current-authority handling after revocation is not defined.
findings.closure_criterion: Omit the hook and launch visibly after expiry, before issuance, and after terminal/rewind => Import records UNAUTHORIZED_DISPATCH and refuses acceptance in every case; Reserve, revoke/expire before launch, replay, then reconcile => Historical reservation remains counted; it grants no new launch eligibility; any stale launch blocks closure; Launch a valid reserved job and leave another reservation unlaunched => Valid launch imports; unused reservation stays counted without a false failure

fix.action: Define the declared namespace/controller set independently of lease validity. Enumerate all associated runs, then check each actual start against the reservation, approved unit/route/baseline, and authority interval. Separate historical reservation lookup from a current launch_allowed result. Require controller refusal on invalid current authority; at import detect and block any launch that slipped through after expiry/revocation.
fix.why: Detect every observed implementation launch associated with the HMA-bound controller/unit, including launches outside valid authority intervals. A late, revoked or unreserved launch must append a closure-blocking finding. Historical replay must not represent fresh launch permission.

verification.method: Omit the hook and launch visibly after expiry, before issuance, and after terminal/rewind
verification.expected: Import records UNAUTHORIZED_DISPATCH and refuses acceptance in every case

fix.tradeoffs: This is detection within the trusted-host boundary. It does not require preventing a hostile same-UID host or scanning undisclosed namespaces. Retain append-only counts for unknown launches.
fix.alternative: Initially use a run-owned HMA-bound namespace and require complete namespace reconciliation at every import/closure. Refuse indeterminate association until the host repairs it.

The eligible independent route launches P, writes a pass report with explicit resolution of F1, then fails (or a host option drift launches the worker in write mode). The named v4 predicates still pass, so the pass verdict can become APPROVE and the apparent F1 resolution can clear a BLOCK. No host forgery is required. This variant requires an importer that does not additionally bind the report body to the current packet; v4 does not specify that check.

findings.title: All-ledger-runs reconciliation conflicts with review accounting
findings.diagnosis: The new scan says every ledger run starting inside the lease window must map one-to-one to an implementation reservation. The retained budget rule says reviews are not implementation attempts. V4 does not prohibit a legitimate review from using the same ledger namespace or define a separate review authorization class in this scan. Such a review either creates a false UNAUTHORIZED_DISPATCH finding or is charged as an implementation attempt.

evidence.observation: Every ledger run in the namespace/window must map to a reservation.
Review launches are excluded from implementation attempts, while per-change independent reviews can occur inside an active lease.
A valid same-namespace review without an implementation reservation is flagged by the literal all-runs filter.

findings.reproduction_or_attack: 1. Reserve and launch implementation I. 2. During the same active lease, launch its approved independent review R in the declared namespace. 3. Do not debit R as an implementation attempt, as v2 requires. 4. Import: R has no implementation reservation, so the literal v4 all-runs rule emits UNAUTHORIZED_DISPATCH. Debiting R to silence the error instead consumes the wrong budget.
findings.expected: Reconcile both implementation and review launches against their appropriate authorizations. Review launches must neither disappear from provenance checks nor debit implementation-attempt counters.
findings.actual: The new scan says every ledger run starting inside the lease window must map one-to-one to an implementation reservation. The retained budget rule says reviews are not implementation attempts. V4 does not prohibit a legitimate review from using the same ledger namespace or define a separate review authorization class in this scan. Such a review either creates a false UNAUTHORIZED_DISPATCH finding or is charged as an implementation attempt.
findings.closure_criterion: Run one implementation plus one legitimate independent review in the permitted namespace arrangement => One implementation attempt charged; both launches authorized; no false BLOCK; Add an unapproved review or relabel an implementation as review => Import refuses the unauthorized launch; role labels alone cannot bypass attempt accounting

fix.action: Tag ledger associations by HMA run/unit/controller and operation role. Map implementation launches to attempt reservations and reviews to approved review dispatches/receipts. Alternatively, require distinct implementation/review namespaces and make that separation an explicit checked contract. Add a negative fixture for an unapproved review, too.
fix.why: Reconcile both implementation and review launches against their appropriate authorizations. Review launches must neither disappear from provenance checks nor debit implementation-attempt counters.

verification.method: Run one implementation plus one legitimate independent review in the permitted namespace arrangement
verification.expected: One implementation attempt charged; both launches authorized; no false BLOCK

verification.method: Add an unapproved review or relabel an implementation as review
verification.expected: Import refuses the unauthorized launch; role labels alone cannot bypass attempt accounting

fix.tradeoffs: A role-aware scan needs an authenticated association; trusting worker-supplied role text would recreate the gap. Separate namespaces are simpler but require explicit inventory and path binding.
fix.alternative: Use a checked implementation-only ledger namespace, with separate pinned review namespace and independent reconciliation.
